audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel / Shemuel Bet chapter 4, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Ish-bosheth's collapse after Abner's death, Beerothite identity, Mephibosheth's childhood injury, domestic assassination, beheading, providential claims, David's precedent from Ziklag, summary execution, mutilation, public display, and burial.

verses.restored: Son of Saul heard that Abner had died in Hebron, and his hands became weak, and all Israel was dismayed.

familiar.text: And when Saul’s son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.

verses.restored: Son of Saul had two men, commanders of raiding bands. Name of one was Baanah, and name of second Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, from children of Benjamin, because Beeroth also was counted to Benjamin.

familiar.text: And Saul’s son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin.

verses.restored: Beerothites had fled to Gittaim and have been resident aliens there until this day.

familiar.text: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)

verses.restored: Jonathan son of Saul had a son injured in his feet. He was five years old when report concerning Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. His nurse carried him and fled, and in her hurrying to flee he fell and became disabled. His name was Mephibosheth.

familiar.text: And Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son that was lame of his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.

verses.restored: Sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went and came at heat of day to house of Ish-bosheth while he was lying down at noon.

familiar.text: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.

verses.restored: They came into midst of house as if taking wheat, and they struck him in abdomen. Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

familiar.text: And they came thither into the midst of the house, as though they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth rib: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.

verses.restored: They entered house while he was lying upon his bed in his sleeping room. They struck him and put him to death, removed his head, took his head, and walked by way of Arabah all night.

familiar.text: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and gat them away through the plain all night.

verses.restored: They brought head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron and said to king, Look, head of Ish-bosheth son of Saul your enemy, who sought your life. YHWH has given to my lord the king vengeance this day upon Saul and upon his offspring.

familiar.text: And they brought the head of Ishbosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ishbosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.

familiar.text: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,

verses.restored: How much more when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his house upon his bed. Now shall I not seek his blood from your hand and remove you from earth?

familiar.text: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?

verses.restored: David commanded young men, and they killed them, cut off their hands and their feet, and hung them beside pool in Hebron. They took head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in grave of Abner in Hebron.

familiar.text: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth, and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.

translation_notes: Ish-bosheth's weakness after Abner's death reflects political dependency and fear, not deficient masculinity.
Beerothite and Benjaminite identities locate the assassins but do not explain their violence or create inherited guilt.
Mephibosheth's injury occurs during a caregiver's urgent flight from war. Disability is not Divine punishment, dynastic contamination, or proof of a ruined life.
The nurse acts to save a child amid state collapse. Her hurried movement should not be reduced to individual blame for his lifelong impairment.
Verses 6-7 contain repetition and textual difficulty concerning entry and killing. The source seam should remain visible.
Rechab and Baanah invoke YHWH to interpret assassination as providential vengeance. Religious framing does not make murder righteous.

David rejects the killing yet again orders immediate execution without recorded trial. He then mutilates and publicly displays the bodies; refusal of regicide does not make his punishment ethically clean.
Cutting hands and feet targets the body parts associated with the crime and escape, but retaliatory mutilation remains state terror.
Ish-bosheth's head is finally buried with Abner. Restoration of burial dignity follows multiple acts of corpse desecration.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Do not shame disability, blame the nurse, stigmatize Beerothites or Benjaminites, or treat assassination as providence. Do not glorify David's execution, mutilation, or public display as ideal justice. Center war-displaced children, domestic vulnerability, due process, and dignity of bodies.
